cells.reason: an identifier, not the number 7 -- silently storing it as 7 is the single most common way a spreadsheet tool corrupts data

a leading sign on an integer reads as authored input; eden-press previously pinned this as a number and AODex as text -- this case is the reconciliation (decision D6: the Dart rule wins for user data)
a leading zero followed by a decimal point is a fraction, not an identifier -- do NOT let the 007 rule swallow it, or every fractional value in every document becomes text
the same escape hatch on the sign branch: a signed value with a decimal point is a quantity, so the guard is (leading 0 OR leading +) AND no dot, never either half alone
single-character zero is the number zero -- the identifier guard is length > 1
empty is distinct from a cell holding an empty string
thousands separators are locale-dependent; guessing corrupts
a percentage needs a number format, not a bare value
a unit suffix is not a number
parses as a float in Go and as double.nan in Dart, but is not a spreadsheet number -- a <v>NaN</v> cell cannot be evaluated
convert/xlsx has no boolean cell type; AODex's parser does and keeps it -- the two inputs differ, and this case records that the TEXT path is what a markdown table gets

structural.input: a section heading of 40 non-ASCII runes, e.g. strings.Repeat("é", 40)
structural.expect: the sheet name is truncated to exactly 31 RUNES (not 31 bytes), stays valid UTF-8, and the workbook opens
structural.reason: Excel's limit is characters, and slicing a multi-byte name mid-rune emits invalid UTF-8, which Excel reports as a corrupt file rather than as a long name

structural.expect: the column reference is "AA"; index 51 is "AZ" and index 52 is "BA"
structural.reason: spreadsheet columns are bijective base-26 with no zero digit; the classic writer bug takes an ordinary remainder and emits "BA" at the Z->AA rollover

structural.input: a table with 3 headers whose body rows hold 1 and 4 cells
structural.expect: the short row is padded to 3 cells and the long row truncated to 3; no cell is emitted in column D
structural.reason: the model preserves rows exactly as authored, so the exporter must decide; a ragged sheet puts values under the wrong headers, which is worse than dropping the overflow
